why: Several commits leave real choices. Commit 4 must decide which product saves reach only one product ('if the action cannot tell these apart … add a reach field and decide on it') and convert about 55 store-wide catalogTag refreshes to refreshCatalog(); its own text first offers and then withdraws dropping catalogTag from getProduct(). Commit 2 picks between a limit and a SQL percentile rewrite for speed samples and may have to design paging plus a 'Show earlier messages' control for the AI manager. Commit 5 reorders reads on the cart and checkout, the pay path. A slip in the VAT CTE, the cache tags or the waves touches money and staleness in ways the equality test and e2e only partly cover.
harm_if_wrong: A product page could keep showing an old price or stock after a store-wide price, VAT or shipping change (a missed refreshCatalog), or a listing could show a wrong VAT-inclusive price, while the named tests pass.
make_it_cheaper: Split the step: give commit 1 (VAT CTE and alt join) and commit 3 (bounded home and metadata) as their own cheap-then-review briefs, and in commit 4 list each products/actions.ts action with its reach and every refreshTag(catalogTag(...)) call site with its replacement; commit 2 should fix the speed-samples choice to 'limit 20000' and state whether the chat already pages.
brief_problems: Commit 4's getProduct() instruction contradicts itself ('REMOVE catalogTag(storeId) … only if …; the safe form … drops catalogTag(storeId)'), and catalogWideTag appears with no export named alongside productTag and catalogListsTag.
About 55 call sites refresh catalogTag(...) today; 'change refreshTag(catalogTag(storeId)) wherever it is used store-wide' gives the cheap model no list and no rule for which are store-wide.
vat_category is NOT NULL with default 'standard' (schema.ts:2611), so the 'if vat_category can be null' branch is moot and could mislead.
Commit 5 depends on steps 0.22, 1.9, 1.11 and 2.13 (perRequest cart facts, statement log with values hash, scripts/server-budget.mjs, buy facts), whose shapes are assumed.
